title: cs-qbr-tiering-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a compact, operational customer segmentation sheet and associated playbooks to prioritize QBRs and renewal activities. It's designed to be lightweight (sheet + short playbook) that CSMs and CS managers can use during weekly planning, renewal foreshadowing, and exec QBR prep.

Overview of segmentation approach (one pager):
- Goal: convert noisy signals across ARR, product fit, deployment type, region and health into a single actionable prioritization band for QBRs and renewal outreach.
- Outcome: top-of-stack customers get allocated proactive time (exec QBRs, renewals AE involvement) while mid/low band customers get scaled playbooks (health campaigns, product workshops).

Segmentation dimensions and scoring (numeric rubric):
1) ARR / revenue tier (0-40 points)
   - >$2.5M ARR = 40
   - $500k-$2.5M = 25
   - $100k-$500k = 12
   - <$100k = 4
2) ICP fit (0-25 points) — product/industry alignment, strategic referenceability
   - Strategic anchor customer (vertical match + reference potential) = 25
   - Good fit (core ICP, repeatable use-case) = 15
   - Some fit (one-off use-case) = 6
   - Poor fit = 0
3) Deployment mode & data sensitivity (0-15 points)
   - Private / on-prem with SLAs = 15
   - Dedicated / reserved capacity = 10
   - Hosted API only = 5
4) Region priority (0-5 points)
   - HQ region with strategic focus (NA/EMEA/APAC priority) = 5
   - Other = 2
5) Health & adoption score (0-15 points) — composite of usage trends, latency SLA violations, error rate, and eval regressions
   - Growing usage, healthy latency = 15
   - Stable but flat = 8
   - Declining or repeated SLA misses = 2

Total max = 100. Priority bands:
- Band A (85-100): Immediate exec QBR + renewal runway plan; AE/Eng stakeholder alignment.
- Band B (60-84): Structured QBR (CS lead + AM) + targeted enablement and uplift plan.
- Band C (35-59): Product workshop + health campaign; no exec unless risk.
- Band D (<35): Automation-first outreach; churn prevention playbooks.

Operational playbooks per band (concise actions):
- Band A playbook:
  * Timeline: Start renewal runway 9 months out; schedule executive QBR 6 months out.
  * Stakeholders: CSM, Account Exec, Solutions Eng, Customer Success Manager, Head of Customer Success.
  * Assets to prepare: tailored ROI slide, infra performance summary, risk register, carrier/region capacity plan.
  * Special actions: pre-approve discounts internally, surface Dedicated/Private offering if cost/perf alignment is weak, schedule 1:1 with VP Customer.

- Band B playbook:
  * Timeline: Run renewal checklist at 6 months; QBR 3 months out.
  * Stakeholders: CSM, AM, Solutions Eng.
  * Assets: usage snapshot, model quality light audit (promptset + evals), cost saving suggestions from Optimize.
  * Actions: organize product workshop, confirm roadmap alignment, propose pricing tiering options.

- Band C playbook:
  * Timeline: Monitor monthly; proactive outreach 3 months before renewal.
  * Stakeholders: CSM, CS Ops.
  * Assets: health remediation plan, onboarding refresh materials, automated success playbooks.
  * Actions: enroll customer in adoption campaign, offer office hours.

- Band D playbook:
  * Timeline: Automated checks + light-touch emails 90 days before renewal.
  * Stakeholders: CSM (shared), Rev Ops.
  * Assets: self-serve guides, FAQ, renewal self-serve options.
  * Actions: triggered churn script, propose switch to pay-as-you-go or pause options.

Scoring mechanics and data sources (where numbers come from):
- ARR: billing system (Finance export) — latest 30d invoice run.
- ICP fit: sales/solutions tags on account record + AE / CSM qualitative flag (enum: anchor/good/some/poor).
- Deployment mode: infra inventory table (dedicated/private/hosted).
- Region: billing address + primary product usage region.
- Health score: computed in CS metrics sheet using weighted signals: weekly active tokens, error rate >0.5%, mean latency delta, eval regressions.

Minimum viable sheet layout (text-first; single sheet columns):
- Account | ARR | ICP_flag | Deploy_mode | Region | Health_score | Total_score | Priority_band | Renewal_date | Next_action | Owner | Notes
Example rows (pipe-delimited):
- "AtlasRetail | 1,800,000 | anchor | dedicated | NA | 12 | 82 | Band B | 2026-09-10 | Schedule QBR + workshop | Priya Shah | runway starts 2026-03"
- "BlueHealth | 3,200,000 | anchor | private | EMEA | 14 | 99 | Band A | 2027-01-18 | Exec QBR + AE align | Marco Ruiz | potential upsell: private SLA"
- "GardenApps | 85,000 | some | hosted | NA | 6 | 27 | Band D | 2026-07-01 | Automated renewal email | Owen Blake | low usage; encourage sandbox adoption"

QBR agenda templates (short):
- Executive QBR (Band A): 1) Business outcomes & metrics, 2) Platform performance & reliability (latency/cost), 3) Strategic roadmap & integration asks, 4) Renewal & commercial options, 5) Actions & owners.
- Standard QBR (Band B/C): 1) Adoption highlights, 2) Health & risk, 3) Product asks, 4) Next steps + enablement.

Renewal negotiation guide (cheat-sheet):
- When to escalate pricing concessions: only for Band A with >$2M ARR or strategic reference value.
- Typical concessions play: commit to Dedicated capacity vs hosted credits, add fixed performance SLAs, expand support hours.
- Discount guardrails: approval required if >10% discount or >$200k ARR impact.

Open questions / to validate with Sales and Finance:
- Should Private deployment always add +5 to score for strategic weighting? (Finance may push different list pricing).
- Agree on exact health metric weights (token usage vs latency vs eval regressions).
- Finalize renewal runway windows for mid-market accounts.

Next steps (owner-level):
- [Lena] Sync with Revenue Ops to automate ARR pull (due 2026-03-12).
- [Priya] Validate ICP flag mapping with Sales (due 2026-03-05).
- [Marco] Draft exec QBR one-pager template and link into sheet (due 2026-03-18).

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally compact; goal is to land something we can operationalize in the CS sheet next week. Feedback loop: comment inline or flag on Slack #cs-qbr-prep.
